title: Audit logs & admin activity review - Nimbus Financial
next_steps: Sofia to share SOC 2 Type II summary and security whitepaper
Liam to send sample audit-logs export (CSV + JSON) and retention options
Nimbus to confirm required retention window and regulatory controls by 2026-11-20
Schedule follow-up demo of private export and KMS flow (week of 2026-11-23)
action_items: Liam Chen: Export sample (audit-logs-sample.json, audit-logs-sample.csv) and send via secure link (due 2026-11-16)
Sofia Martinez: Share SOC 2 Type II report overview and SSP pointers (due 2026-11-15)
Raj Patel: Confirm retention policy requirement and data residency constraints (due 2026-11-20)
summary: Redwood walked Nimbus through audit logging and admin activity capabilities. Key topics: what events are captured (user/admin actions, API calls, model inference metadata, KMS events), export formats and destinations (S3, secure syslog, Splunk/Datadog integrations), retention controls, immutable retention vs soft delete, and encryption/KMS options. Nimbus requested sample exports and retention pricing and asked about private export flow for on-prem SIEM and VPC egress. Action items agreed and follow-up demo to validate KMS integration and export pipeline.
transcript:
[00:00] Sofia Martinez: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, um today we want to focus on audit logs and admin activity, make sure we cover what you need for audits and regs.
[00:08] Raj Patel: Thanks Sofia, yeah high level we need to know exactly what's captured, retention options, and how to export to our SIEM, we're evaluating retention windows 7 years down to 1 year depending on the event type.
[00:20] Liam Chen: Great, quick intro — I'm Liam, I'm the SE on this account. We'll go through event categories, sample payloads, and the export mechanisms. Apologies in advance if transcripts mishear some of the product names, it's often K-V cache or K-V cash in notes, but it's KV cache.
[00:35] Maya Thompson: Important for us: PII redaction, and whether logs include prompt text or only metadata.
[00:42] Liam Chen: Yeah good call. So by default audit logs capture admin actions (user create/delete, role changes, SSO config), service API calls (model selection, route, tokens used counts), and operational metadata — timestamps, requester IP, region, model variant, sequence length, token counts, and outcome codes.
[00:58] Liam Chen: For sensitive data — we have configurable redaction. Full request bodies (prompts) are captured only if you opt-in for deep-audit mode; otherwise we record a hashed identifier and metadata. Deep-audit mode is typically used for evals or debug, and is configurable per-route.
[01:15] Raj Patel: Ok so default is metadata only, deep mode optional. For compliance we might need to capture some prompt bodies for investigatory trails, but need encryption at rest and key control.
[01:25] Sofia Martinez: Yep, we support customer-managed KMS for Redwood Private and Dedicated customers. You can bring your own key via KMS/HSM — we store wrapped keys and audit the key usage. For hosted customers we offer a managed KMS option but can also do a bring-your-own-key flow under an enterprise contract.
[01:42] Evan Ruiz: Does Redwood log KMS events — like key unwrap calls and who invoked the unwrapping?
[01:46] Liam Chen: Yes, key usage events are emitted to the audit log: key ID, operation (encrypt/decrypt/sign), requester identity and service principal, and timestamp. For Private deployments, those logs can be forwarded to your KMS audit channel as well.
[02:00] Maya Thompson: Export options? We use Splunk and S3 buckets for long term.
[02:04] Liam Chen: We support multiple export sinks: S3 (encrypted SSE-KMS or SSE-C), secure syslog/TCP (for SIEM), direct Splunk HTTP Event Collector (HEC) integration, and a Datadog or Sumo Logic connector. Exports can be near-real-time stream or daily batched dumps.
[02:21] Raj Patel: For S3, can you do object immutability / legal hold? Our retention policy requires immutability for certain event classes.
[02:27] Liam Chen: Yes — when exporting to S3 you can enable object lock (WORM) if using AWS S3 with object lock. We also support export into a write-once destination in private deployments where retention and legal hold policies are enforced at the customer side.
[02:42] Sofia Martinez: Also, in Redwood Console there's a retention policy UI where you can set different retention for admin actions vs inference payloads; and we also have a legal hold flag you can flip which prevents deletion until released by a super-admin.
[02:58] Raj Patel: How granular are event categories? Can we keep admin actions indefinitely but purge inference metadata after 1 year?
[03:04] Liam Chen: Exactly. Retention is per-event-class. We ship with defaults (admin events: 7 years, inference metadata: 1 year, request bodies: 90 days if enabled) but you can customize per-account.
[03:16] Lena Ortiz: What about RBAC? If someone is removed, do their historical actions remain attributed?
[03:20] Liam Chen: Yes, audit logs are immutable for attribution. We store the actor identity at time of event, including SSO subject ID and role at time of action. If a user is deleted, their historical actions still show their user ID and a note that the account was later deprovisioned.
[03:34] Raj Patel: SSO integration — we use Okta. How does that reflect in logs?
[03:37] Liam Chen: We capture SSO provider, SAML subject, and mapping to Redwood user. Login events, MFA events, and successful/failed sign-ins are all logged. Also role changes via SCIM/SSO sync are recorded as admin events.
[03:49] Evan Ruiz: Are logs tamper-evident? We need evidence of integrity for audit.
[03:53] Liam Chen: For Hosted and Dedicated we provide signed log bundles — every daily export has a signature and a chain-of-trust header you can validate. For Private, you manage the signing; the Redwood runtime can write logs with an append-only ledger and provide merkle proofs on request.
[04:07] Maya Thompson: Nice. What about retention pricing and egress? Large export windows could be expensive.
[04:12] Sofia Martinez: Good point — retention beyond the included base (90 days) is tiered and egress for continuous exports is priced by throughput. We'll include retention pricing in the deck.
[04:21] Raj Patel: Sample payloads would be super helpful — can you show an example of admin-change event and an inference-call event?
[04:26] Liam Chen: Sure — I'll attach examples in the follow-up. Short form: admin-change event includes event_type, actor_id, actor_email, target_resource, before/after, timestamp, request_id. Inference-call event includes event_type, request_id, model, model_variant, token_count, latency_ms, region, requester_ip, and if enabled, a prompt_hash or prompt_snippet.
[04:46] Raj Patel: Prompt_snippet is redacted by default right?
[04:49] Liam Chen: By default only hash and metadata. Prompt_snippet is opt-in and can be encrypted server-side with your KMS key.
[04:55] Evan Ruiz: For compliance we might need to run regular exports into our SIEM and have an immutable copy. Is there an automated connector?
[05:00] Liam Chen: Yes, Splunk HEC, syslog over TLS, and native S3 exports are the typical pattern. We also support a webhook-style forwarder for custom ingestion. Exports are batched or streamed with checkpointing so you can replay if an ingestion fails.
[05:16] Raj Patel: Because we operate in EU, we need data residency for logs too. Can exports be region-restricted?
[05:21] Sofia Martinez: You can pin log storage regionally as part of a Private or Dedicated deployment; hosted customers can select region for exports. For EU-only residency we recommend Dedicated in a eu-west-1 region or Private deployment in your VPC.
[05:33] Maya Thompson: A question about search and investigation — are logs queryable in Console? Or do we need to pull to Splunk?
[05:39] Liam Chen: Console has an audit search with filters for actor, event_type, date range, request_id and you can view event JSON. For heavy ad-hoc analytics we suggest exporting into your analytics/SIEM. Console search is intended for triage and quick investigations.
[05:55] Raj Patel: OK. Can retention be enforced at the object-level for S3 exports so we can meet e-discovery holds?
[06:00] Liam Chen: Yes, as mentioned object lock / legal hold is supported on S3 exports, and for Private deployments you can configure immutable storage on-prem or in a customer-managed bucket.
[06:12] Evan Ruiz: Any limitations around PI or GDPR requests? If a user asks for deletion, how do you handle logs?
[06:18] Sofia Martinez: Good question. We separate operational audit from personal data. For GDPR erasure requests we scrub identifiers used to identify a natural person where allowed, and we offer pseudonymization for logs. For immutable legal holds, we coordinate deletion exceptions with your legal team because you may be required to retain certain records. We'll surface the policy and controls in the SOC 2 docs.
[06:38] Raj Patel: For the KMS bring-your-own-key — does Redwood ever get direct access to the plaintext keys?
[06:43] Liam Chen: No, we never persist plaintext customer keys. Keys are used via KMS APIs for cryptographic operations and we store only wrapped keys. For HSM integrations in Private mode, keys stay in your HSM. We log key usage as audit events but not the plaintext key material.
[06:58] Maya Thompson: Do you support key rotation and how is that handled for historical logs?
[07:02] Liam Chen: Key rotation is supported. For historical logs encrypted under prior keys we keep wrapped keys in the key-ring so you can still decrypt historic exports. For strict separation you can enable key-rotation-with-archive where old keys are archived under customer control. We'll include the key rotation doc in the follow-up.
[07:18] Raj Patel: Can you walk through a demo of exporting a day's logs to our S3 with object lock in a follow-up?
[07:22] Sofia Martinez: Yes, that's part of the next steps — Liam will show the sample export flow and we'll schedule a demo for your infra team.
[07:28] Lena Ortiz: Anything about rate limits on export or throttling? We need high throughput for near-real-time exports.
[07:33] Liam Chen: We support high-throughput streaming export on Dedicated/Private. Hosted has throughput SLAs and can scale via reserved capacity; continuous export throughput is a configurable option. We'll include throughput numbers in the export sample file.
[07:46] Raj Patel: One last thing — do you provide a retention report for auditors that shows what was purged vs retained over time?
[07:50] Liam Chen: Yes, Redwood Console can generate retention and deletion audit reports showing event counts per class, retention rules applied, and any legal holds. Those reports are downloadable and we can include them in the SOC 2 artifact pack.
[08:05] Sofia Martinez: Great, recapping next steps: share SOC2 docs, send sample audit log exports, confirm Nimbus retention windows, and schedule follow-up export demo. Anything else?
[08:14] Raj Patel: That covers it, thanks.
[08:16] Sofia Martinez: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with links.
[08:20] [END OF TRANSCRIPT]
